newsitem.title: Australia: Australian fires kill at least one, 800 evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Australian fires kill at least one, 800 evacuated.

text.p: At least one person was killed on Tuesday in huge bushfires that raged throughout the day near the southern Australian city of Melbourne, forcing the evacuation of at least 800 people, police and firefighters said.
"One person is confirmed perished and possibly a second," Victoria police spokeswoman Nicole Hughes told Reuters.
About 10 fires broke out across the state of Victoria, with the worst fronts spread over the Dandenong mountain range, some 30 km (19 miles) east of Melbourne, destroying 44 homes.

At the height of the Dandenong fires, about 700 firefighters battled six major blazes fuelled by dry northerly winds and forests left parched by several days of temperatures nearing 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit).
The cause of the fires was not immediately known.
As darkness fell, changing winds associated with an emerging cold front threatened to force the flames toward more densely populated areas.
But the Bureau of Meteorology said the winds had abated and were expected to be followed by rain within a few hours.
"The wind change...has moved across most of the fire areas and has dropped temperatures quite significantly and there's rain to come," senior forecaster Robert Hooke told Reuters.
Spot fires continued to break out but were under control, the Country Fire Authority (CFA) said.
"The break-outs are disappointing...but I think generally the CFA are on on top of it. I don't think it's out of control," CFA spokesman James Tonkin told Reuters.
Two other major blazes burning to the west and southeast of Melbourne have largely been contained. One of the fires forced firefighters to run for their lives as flames engulfed their water tanker.

The ferocity of Tuesday's fires evoked memories of the 1983 Ash Wednesday disaster in which blazes across Victoria and the neighbouring state of South Australia killed 76 people and burnt more than 2,400 houses to the ground.

Melbourne has been suffering one of the worst heatwaves in a decade. National communications carrier Telstra Corp said its triple-zero emergency telephone lines had been jammed with calls about the fires.
